articles.title: “We’ve been able to raise more funds and continue to grow”: How Andre Agassi and Steffi Graf turned 20 limited-edition watches into $300,000 for charity
articles.summary: Andre Agassi and Steffi Graf celebrated 10 years with Swiss watchmaker Longines in 2018 with a fundraiser that brought in $300,000 for their charities.
articles.body: Andre Agassi and Steffi Graf celebrated 10 years with Swiss watchmaker Longines in 2018 with a fundraiser that brought in $300,000 for their charities. The tennis legends marked the anniversary with a limited-edition watch collection, but the real story was where the money went. The auction supported Agassi’s education foundation and Graf’s Children for Tomorrow, which helps children and families affected by war, exile and violence.The project brought together two causes the couple had supported for years. Agassi focused on educational opportunities for disadvantaged young people in the United States, while Graf’s foundation worked with children dealing with trauma. Later that year, Graf explained how the Longines partnership had helped her charity reach more children and expand its work into schools.How a limited-edition watch auction raised $300,000 for charityLongines unveiled the special Conquest V.H.P. collection at a charity gala at Paris’s Musée Rodin on June 2, 2018. The event honoured Agassi and Graf and celebrated a decade of partnership with the Swiss watchmaker. The collection featured 10 men’s watches and 10 women’s watches, created in limited numbers for the occasion.Longines then held an online auction throughout June. The company kept the first numbered set, marked 1/10, for its museum in Saint-Imier, Switzerland. Buyers acquired the remaining nine sets, and the auction raised $300,000 for the couple’s foundations.The proceeds went to the Andre Agassi Foundation for Education and Children for Tomorrow. Agassi’s foundation works to improve educational opportunities for disadvantaged young people, while Graf established Children for Tomorrow in 1998 to help children and families affected by war, violence and persecution.The fundraiser also reflected how the couple’s relationship with Longines had grown beyond a commercial partnership. Per Las Vegas Sun, Agassi said, “It was built around an overlap of shared values.” He explained that Longines first supported his former Grand Slam for Children event in Las Vegas before the relationship grew over the years.Steffi Graf says Longines helped her charity reach more childrenGraf offered a closer look at the impact of that support in the same Las Vegas Sun interview. At the time, she said Children for Tomorrow helped a little over 1,000 children each year, mostly through therapy.“We’ve been able to raise more funds and continue to grow, and now we are able to go into schools and work with teachers and train teachers to understand trauma. We just have a bigger reach now,” Graf said.Along with therapy, it had begun reaching children through schools and training teachers to recognise trauma. Graf also spoke about the sharp rise in refugees arriving in Germany over the previous five or six years, which brought new challenges involving different languages, cultures and the experiences children had endured.Graf, who founded the charity in 1998, continued to travel to Germany every couple of months to support its work. Longines’ backing helped the organisation raise more funds and extend its reach, she explained.Agassi pursued a different route through education. His charitable work in Las Vegas included the college preparatory campus he established in 2001 to help disadvantaged students access better educational opportunities.The auction brought their separate missions together through one fundraising effort. The $300,000 raised from the watch sale supported both foundations, giving the couple’s anniversary a purpose beyond tennis and luxury watches.The fundraiser continued beyond the June auction. In Nov. 2018, Agassi welcomed winning bidders to Democracy Prep at the Agassi Campus in Las Vegas. articles.title: Los Juegos del Agua cierran en Melilla una edición que ha unido Deporte, territorio y futuro
articles.standfirst: Finalizan tres semanas de competición, organizada por la Asociación del Deporte Español, el Gobierno de la Ciudad Autónoma de Melilla y 11 Federaciones Deportivas Españolas
articles.summary: Finalizan tres semanas de competición, organizada por la Asociación del Deporte Español, el Gobierno de la Ciudad Autónoma de Melilla y 11 Federaciones Deportivas Españolas
articles.body: Con el Campeonato de Europa de Triatlón Youth, Melilla cierra tres semanas de una gran celebración del Deporte Acuático. Los II Juegos del Agua, organizados por la Asociación del Deporte Español (ADESP), el Gobierno de la Ciudad Autónoma de Melilla y 11 Federaciones Deportivas Españolas, han concluido este domingo tras reunir a deportistas, técnicos y jueces de distintas nacionalidades europeas en competiciones nacionales e internacionales, exhibiciones y actividades abiertas a la ciudadanía. Los Juegos han sido mucho más que una sucesión de campeonatos. Han convertido a Melilla en un escaparate de turismo deportivo, han generado actividad económica y social, y han acercado el Deporte de alto nivel a sociedad local y visitantes. La implicación de ADESP y del Gobierno de Melilla ha permitido articular un proyecto que une instituciones, Federaciones, clubes, voluntariado y ciudadanía en torno al mar y al Deporte. Las 11 Federaciones participantes han sido la Real Federación Española de Natación, la Real Federación Española de Piragüismo, la Federación Española de Triatlón, la Federación Española de Surfing, la Real Federación Española de Vela, la Real Federación Española de Motonáutica, la Federación Española de Actividades Subacuáticas, la Real Federación Española de Salvamento y Socorrismo, la Federación Española de Pentatlón Moderno, la Federación Española de Pesca y Casting y la Federación Española de Esquí Náutico y Wakeboard. El Consejero de Educación, Juventud y Deporte de la Ciudad Autónoma de Melilla, Miguel Ángel Fernández Bonnemaisón, ha destacado que “Melilla ha vivido tres semanas de Deporte, ilusión y compromiso. Los Juegos del Agua han permitido mostrar al conjunto de España nuestra capacidad organizativa, nuestra riqueza natural y la pasión de nuestra gente por el Deporte”. Por su parte, José Hidalgo, Presidente de ADESP, ha agradecido “la implicación de la Ciudad de Melilla, de las 11 Federaciones participantes y de todos los agentes que han hecho posible esta cita. Melilla ha demostrado su capacidad para acoger eventos de alto nivel y para convertir el Deporte en una herramienta de proyección, desarrollo y futuro”. Dos historias resumen el espíritu de la cita. La primera es la de Agüín, la mascota de los Juegos, que ha recorrido escenarios, actos y colegios de Melilla. A través del programa educativo Guardianes del Mar, ha llegado a 17 centros educativos y 22 representaciones para más de dos mil estudiantes, transmitiendo valores de respeto por el mar, responsabilidad ambiental y cercanía a los Deportes acuáticos. La segunda es la del trofeo del Campeonato de Europa de Stand Up Paddle que se celebró al inicio de estos Juegos, diseñado y creado por Américo Correa con madera de deriva, restos reutilizados y materiales recuperados. Entre ellos, la base del trofeo procede de una palmatoria fabricada por un herrero en Melilla hace más de 40 años, que regresó a la ciudad tras décadas en otras latitudes peninsulares. Y después de unas 35 horas de trabajo, el trofeo encarna la filosofía de reducir, reutilizar y reciclar. Su historia conecta con la bandera Green Sport Flag, el proyecto del Deporte Español en favor del medioambiente promovido por ADESP y que ha estado presente durante los Juegos como símbolo de una competición que cuida el mar, reduce su impacto y educa en sostenibilidad. Melilla cierra así una edición que ha demostrado que el Deporte puede ser motor de desarrollo, identidad y futuro.

articles.title: España, decimosexta por equipos en el Mundial y sin finalistas por aparatos
articles.standfirst: Ray Zapata e Ignacio Yockers no estarán en las finales de suelo ni caballo con arcos y tampoco habrá españoles en la final de concurso completo
articles.summary: Ray Zapata e Ignacio Yockers no estarán en las finales de suelo ni caballo con arcos
articles.body: El equipo español masculino de gimnasia artística acabó en decimosexta posición en la calificación del Mundial, que se disputa estos días en Rotterdam. Así, Daniel Carrión, Thierno Diallo, Nicolau Mir, Joel Plata, Ray Zapata e Ignacio Yockers sumaron 235.329 puntos, insuficientes para entrar a la final a la que accedían los ocho primeros, cuyo corte estableció Colombia (242.727), que alcanza su primera final mundialista por equipos. Lidera la clasificación Japón, campeona del mundo en 2023, con 254.529. España tampoco logró clasificar ningún gimnasta para la final de concurso completo, a la que pasaron los 24 mejores. Ignacio Yockers fue el mejor español, en el puesto 33, con 77.832 puntos (cuarto reserva). El japonés Oka Shinnosuke, vigente campeón olímpico de la especialidad, firmó la mejor actuación, con 85.098 puntos. En las finales individuales, Ray Zapata e Ignacio Yockers no podrán luchar por las medallas en suelo ni caballo con arcos, respectivamente. El subcampeón olímpico, que ha estado preparando en Panamá a las órdenes de Carlos Gil el Mundial con el horizonte puesto en los Juegos, finalizó decimoséptimo, con 13.700 puntos, tras algunas imprecisiones en la recepción de una de las diagonales. El ruso Dukhno Arsenii, subcampeón en suelo en el reciente Europeo, obtuvo la mayor puntuación, con 14.700. Por su parte, Yockers, quinto en los últimos Europeos, finalizó undécimo en la calificación de caballo con arcos, con 14.300 (tercer reserva), prueba que dominó el armenio Manukyan Hamlet, plata continental en esta especialidad el pasado agosto.

articles.title: Indus Valley motifs feature on blazers as India brings 5,000 years of heritage to Para Asian Games opening ceremony
articles.summary: The Indian contingent brought a glimpse of the country's 5,000-year-old heritage to the opening ceremony of the Para Asian Games on Sunday, with athletes
articles.body: The Indian contingent brought a glimpse of the country's 5,000-year-old heritage to the opening ceremony of the Para Asian Games on Sunday, with athletes wearing ceremonial blazers featuring motifs inspired by ancient Indian civilisation.More than 100 Indian athletes took part in the ceremony, led by Paralympic medallist sprinter Simran Sharma and top shuttler Pramod Bhagat, who carried the national flag as the contingent marched with the Tricolour.The ceremonial blazers featured prints of seals from the Indus Valley, drawing on the ancient script and motifs of one of the world's oldest civilisations.“Team India walked out wearing more than just ceremonial dress -- they wore 5,000 years of civilisation. The Indian contingent’s ceremonial blazer is a tribute to our heritage,” the Paralympic Committee of India said.The blazers also featured SaptSindhu on the collar, representing the land of the seven rivers and the mighty Saraswati. The Tricolour was prominently displayed on the pocket.India has sent a 281-member contingent to the Games, comprising 168 athletes -- 112 men and 56 women -- who will compete across 11 disciplines.The Games will conclude on October 24, with around 3,000 athletes from 45 nations competing under the motto "Imagine One Heart".India had its most successful Asian Para Games campaign in Hangzhou in 2023, finishing fifth in the medal standings with a record 111 medals, including 29 gold, 31 silver and 51 bronze.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Asian Para Games: Can India’s para-athletes script another 100-medal triumph despite a smaller contingent?
articles.summary: India’s para-athletes will look to build on the country’s remarkable rise in international para-sports as the fifth edition of the Asian Para Games gets
articles.body: India’s para-athletes will look to build on the country’s remarkable rise in international para-sports as the fifth edition of the Asian Para Games gets underway in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, on October 18. After India’s fourth-place finish at the Asian Games 2026, the para contingent will aim to continue the country’s impressive medal-winning run at the continental event.India will be represented by 166 athletes across 10 disciplines at the October 18-24 event. The contingent features several Paralympic medallists, world champions and emerging talents, including archer Sheetal Devi, badminton stars Pramod Bhagat and Suhas Yathiraj, and para-table tennis player Bhavina Patel.India’s recent performances at the Asian Para Games and Paralympics have established the country as an increasingly competitive force in para-sports. From 14 medals at the inaugural edition in 2010 to a record 108 in Hangzhou in 2023, the progress has been remarkable. The challenge in Aichi-Nagoya will be to build on that foundation and demonstrate that the momentum can continue, even with a smaller contingent.Can India cross the 100-medal mark for the second consecutive edition? While the size of this year’s squad makes comparisons with Hangzhou particularly interesting, India’s established medal-winners and growing strength across disciplines provide reasons for optimism.166 athletes across 10 disciplines: India’s medal prospectsIndia’s contingent comprises 111 male and 55 female athletes, alongside 94 team officials and support staff and 15 contingent staff members.Para-athletics accounts for the largest share, with 62 athletes, followed by para-badminton with 28 and para-swimming with 16. Para-shooting has 13 athletes, while para-archery and para-table tennis have 11 and 10, respectively. The remaining disciplines are blind football (10), para-powerlifting (eight), para-judo (seven) and para-cycling (one).The squad brings together established international performers and athletes looking to make their mark at the continental level. Sheetal, Pramod, Suhas and Bhavina are among the prominent names to watch, while para-athletics is expected to play a central role in India’s medal campaign.From 14 medals to 108: India’s remarkable riseIndia’s journey at the Asian Para Games offers a compelling picture of sustained improvement. The country won 14 medals at the inaugural edition in 2010, comprising one gold, four silver and nine bronze, to finish 15th in the standings.Four years later, India retained 15th place but more than doubled its tally, winning 33 medals - three gold, 14 silver and 16 bronze.The breakthrough came in 2018, when India secured 72 medals, including 15 gold, 24 silver and 33 bronze, to climb to ninth place. At Hangzhou in 2023, the contingent took another giant leap, winning 108 medals (27 gold, 32 silver and 49 bronze) to finish fifth.The progression across four editions reflects the growing depth of Indian para-sports:India has improved its medal tally in every edition so far while also making significant gains in the standings. The jump from 72 to 108 medals between the 2018 and 2023 editions was particularly impressive, taking the country past the 100-medal mark for the first time.Aichi-Nagoya offers the next opportunity to extend that progress and build on the foundations established over the previous decade.Paralympic success underlines India’s growing potentialThe rise at the Asian Para Games has been accompanied by a remarkable improvement in India’s performances at the Paralympics.India finished 43rd at the Rio Paralympics in 2016 with four medals. At Tokyo 2020, the country won 19 medals - five gold, eight silver and six bronze - to finish 24th. The momentum continued at Paris 2024, where India achieved its best-ever Paralympic haul of 29 medals, including seven gold, nine silver and 13 bronze, to finish 18th.These results underline the progress made by India’s para-athletes and have helped raise expectations ahead of the Aichi-Nagoya Games.Can India repeat its 100-medal achievement?India’s record-breaking 108-medal performance at Hangzhou has naturally raised expectations ahead of the Aichi-Nagoya Games. However, the contingent this time comprises 166 athletes, compared with 309 at the previous edition.That represents a reduction of 143 athletes, or approximately 46%. The smaller squad makes a repeat of the previous tally a demanding target, but it does not diminish the significance of the opportunity before the contingent.India’s able-bodied athletes also competed with a smaller contingent at the 2026 Asian Games, with the squad size falling from 661 in Hangzhou to 495 in Aichi-Nagoya. India finished with 85 medals (21 gold, 27 silver and 37 bronze) after winning 106 at the previous edition.The 21-medal decline came alongside a reduction of around 25% in the number of athletes. The comparison offers an interesting reference point, although it cannot be directly applied to the para contingent because the two competitions have different event structures, athlete profiles and medal opportunities.If the relationship between contingent size and medal output at the Asian Games were used purely as a mathematical illustration, the 46% reduction in India’s para contingent could suggest a medal tally of around 68. Such a figure, however, would be only a theoretical estimate, not a reliable prediction of the outcome.A more encouraging perspective comes from India’s own history at the Asian Para Games. The country won 72 medals with 211 athletes in 2018 before improving to 108 medals with 309 athletes in 2023. Those results demonstrate that medal conversion depends on far more than the size of the contingent.The quality and competitive experience of the athletes, their event specialisations and their ability to deliver on the day will all influence India’s final tally. A smaller squad can still produce an impressive return if its members make the most of their medal opportunities.Aichi-Nagoya: Another opportunity to raise the barIndia’s fourth-place finish at the Asian Games has provided a positive backdrop for the para contingent, even though the able-bodied athletes’ final tally of 85 medals was below their Hangzhou total of 106.The Asian Para Games present a fresh opportunity for India to underline the breadth of its sporting progress. The country’s para-athletes have steadily improved their medal totals, climbed the continental standings and carried that momentum onto the Paralympic stage.The immediate target will be to produce strong performances across the 10 disciplines and make the most of the opportunities available. A second consecutive 100-medal finish would be a landmark achievement, while another strong overall showing would further consolidate India’s position among Asia’s leading para-sport nations.The numbers suggest that matching Hangzhou will be challenging, but the bigger story is the remarkable journey that has taken India from 14 medals in 2010 to 108 in 2023.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Ari y Ustero, imparables: tres títulos en los últimos cuatro torneos para mirar de frente al número 1
articles.standfirst: Las catalanas siguen reforzando su candidatura y alargan la racha sin títulos de Bea y Paula
articles.summary: Las catalanas siguen reforzando su candidatura al número uno y alargan la racha sin títulos de Bea y Paula
articles.body: El Allianz Cloud acogía las finales del Milano Premier Padel P1 con el cartel de ‘sold out’ en las taquillas del estadio. La pareja formada por González y Josemaría tenía un último obstáculo en su camino de regreso a la victoria: Ustero y Sánchez, verdugos también de las número dos semanas atrás en el P2 de Rotterdam Paula y Bea ya habían dejado claro en los días previos, en la rueda de prensa, que su objetivo pasaba por volver a sentirse competitivas en pista y disfrutar del juego. La victoria se les resistía, pero no era algo que les preocupara. Con esa premisa, firmaron un gran arranque de la final y lograron el primer break tras el paso por banquillos. La ventaja reflejaba lo que sucedía sobre la pista: Ari no conseguía imponer su juego en el cruzado y Andrea no encontraba en la pegada el arma necesaria para hacer daño a sus rivales. Sin embargo, con 5-2 en el marcador, el guion dio un giro. Las pupilas de Ángel González comenzaron a encontrar su ritmo y aprovecharon los errores de sus rivales para recuperar uno de los breaks en el 5-3. El cambio de dinámica se confirmó tras el paso por banquillos, cuando lograron igualar el encuentro. Un golpe duro para la pareja de Gilardoni, que acusó especialmente ese quiebre en el final del primer set. Llegado el tie-break ‘Magic’ Ari tomó las riendas del juego y marcó el ritmo hasta cerrar el desempate con un contundente 7-3. El golpe anímico se prolongó en el inicio del segundo asalto, y Bea y Paula cedieron su servicio en el segundo juego, lo que permitió a sus rivales abrir una brecha de 3-0 en el marcador. La ventaja se mantuvo hasta el final, sin sufrimiento al servicio, y fue suficiente para cerrar el encuentro. A la segunda bola de partido, Ari y Ustero sellaron el definitivo 6-3, conquistando así su quinto título de la temporada y tercero de los últimos cuatro torneos. Un nuevo triunfo que las acerca al número uno del mundo, del que ya les separan tan solo 1.980 puntos en la Race de Premier Padel.

articles.title: Is Caleb Williams playing today? Injury update, fantasy advice for Bears star in Week 6
articles.summary: The Chicago Bears offense receives a massive lift after missing their QB1 over the last three weeks.
articles.body:
The Chicago Bears have an important NFC showdown on Sunday against the Atlanta Falcons, and starting quarterback Caleb Williams appears to be back in the mix.

Head coach Ben Johnson couldn't have asked for better timing with Williams' return with the Bears currently at 3-2 during the 2026 NFL season. The NFC North has proven to be a juggernaut through five weeks, and Chicago's QB1 is vital for their offense.

The former USC Trojans star has only appeared in two games in 2026 after suffering a scary Grade 2 hamstring injury against the Minnesota Vikings. Initial thoughts based on Williams' reaction led to many overreactions.

However, Chicago's been able to survive in the interim with a combination of Case Keenum and Tyler Bagent behind center. That said, the Bears are hopeful that they'll have their biggest offensive weapon on the field in Week 6.

"He's back: The Bears are planning to start Caleb Williams after he missed the past three games due to a torn hamstring but went through a full week of practice this week without any setbacks, per NFLN and ESPN," Schefter said in an X post on Saturday .

Meanwhile, the Bears offense simply isn't the same without him on the field. That goes for top receiving weapons like Rome Odunze, Colston Loveland and Luther Burden.

Williams is a must-start against Atlanta. Both teams possess high-powered offenses that can explode for points. The combination of the Bears star's passing and rushing abilities make him a top candidate to score lots of points on the gridiron and in fantasy this week.

Happy Sunday Husky fans. Russell has shown his versatility during his senior season by kicking out to tackle and dominating so far. Husky coaches are expecting him to remain inside and play center for them, but he should have the versatility to be able to play a guard position if needed in college. When I see his film I see a tenacious blocker who should add some nastiness to the Husky offensive line in the coming years (IMHO they need this).

In the 2028 class the Huskies extended an offer out to 4 star defensive lineman RJ Wyms from the Woodlands College Park HS, in Texas. Wyms, who is currently rated as the 36th best player in the country, and 4th best defensive lineman is an explosive defensive lineman who should lineup as a 5T in college. Most of the top programs in the country are after him and it will be tough for the Huskies to reel in a top defensive lineman from Texas, however they are still active in the state and are looking to grab as much talent as they can from the state of Texas.

That is all for today and as we get information about where Husky coaches travelled over the weekend we will make sure to share that information here. As always follow me @asieverkropp.

articles.title: 'Catch of the Day!': Faheem Ashraf completes sensational relay catch in Rawalpindi to save debutant Saad Baig’s blushes
articles.summary: Faheem Ashraf took a stunning relay catch after debutant keeper Saad Baig spilled the ball, breaking Sri Lanka's opening stand in the Pakistan ODI Tri-Series...
articles.body:
Pakistan's Faheem Ashraf's relay catch dismissed Avishka Fernando after debutant Saad Baig fumbled the chance.

Faheem then removed Kusal Mendis, as Saim Ayub held a sharp catch at point.

Fans were ecstatic to see Ashraf pull off that reflex catch.

From disaster to brilliance! Faheem Ashraf pulls off an incredible catch to break Sri Lanka's opening stand

Catch of the day was the instant verdict in Rawalpindi, where Faheem Ashraf pulled off a sensational relay catch to rescue debutant Saad Baig from what could have been an awkward moment and to break Sri Lanka's opening stand in the ODI tri-series.

Pakistan had batted first in the opening fixture of the tri-nation series and finished with 305 runs on the board. Sri Lanka answered with a calm start, and their openers put together a stand of 30 runs, which suggested that the visitors were comfortable on a good batting surface. However, the contest turned quickly once Naseem Shah began to test the batters with the short ball.

In the sixth over, Naseem pitched a short delivery at Avishka Fernando, who tried to pull it away. The batter was cramped for room, and the shot only produced a top edge that sent the ball steeply into the air towards short fine leg. It was the kind of chance that looks simple from a distance but becomes awkward as it dips under the lights.

Baig, who is keeping wicket on his debut, ran across and got both hands to the ball, but he lost his balance at the crucial moment and the ball popped out of his gloves.

What happened next saved Pakistan a wicket and the young player some embarrassment. Ashraf had positioned himself behind Saad near deep fine leg, and he stayed calm enough to gather the spilled ball and complete a relay catch.

Baig looked visibly relieved, because a miss in his first international outing could easily have turned into a long-remembered blunder.

Fan reactions to Faheem Ashraf's relay catch

@CallMeSheri1_ summed up the incident in a few blunt lines that described how the ball ended up in Faheem's hands.

He wrote: "CATCH OF THE DAY. Saad Baig dropped it, but the ball went straight into the hands of Faheem Ashraf."

@waleed_ch5 was full of praise for the fielding effort and added a set of hashtags for the match.

He wrote: "What a stunning catch by Faheem Ashraf! Absolute brilliance on the field! #PAKvsSL #FaheemAshraf #PakistanCricket #Cricket"

@BasitSubhani took a more critical view of the debutant, though he also had kind words for the fielder who saved the day.

He wrote: "Baig dropped a catch which you expect a wicket keeper to take … He should be thankful to Faheem Ashraf for showing presence of mind who got it at the end!"

Finally, @MianAhmad_56 credited Faheem's positioning for turning a possible misjudgment into a wicket and also pointed out a small milestone for the bowler.

He wrote: "Faheem Ashraf's timely positioning saved a dropped catch or a misjudged chance by debutant Saad Baig. Naseem Shah got his first."

Faheem's awareness turned a debut error into a team win

Fielding rarely receives the praise given to big hundreds or five-wicket hauls, yet moments like this one often decide matches. Faheem Ashraf did not rely on luck here, because a player who places himself behind a teammate is thinking two steps ahead. That kind of awareness is hard to coach, and it is exactly what separates a decent fielding unit from a very good one.

Saad Baig deserves some sympathy, since the ball was dropping awkwardly and he lost his footing while running a long way. Debuts bring nerves, and a fumble of this kind can linger in a young player's mind. However, the fact that a teammate was alert enough to back him up may help him settle quickly, and it shows the sort of support structure Pakistan have built in the field.

Pakistan will be pleased with how the pace attack and the fielders worked together, although they must stay sharper in future games, since a chase of 306 can still turn quickly if the openers are allowed to settle. For now, the early wickets have given the hosts the advantage in this tri-series opener.

articles.title: Browns get bad news on RB Quinshon Judkins for Week 6 vs. Ravens
articles.summary: This news for the Browns is a tough blow for their Week 6 matchup.
articles.body:
The Cleveland Browns are facing off against the Baltimore Ravens in Week 6, with a chance to retake the AFC North lead with a win over their division rivals.

While the Ravens will be without Lamar Jackson, the Browns got some bad news of their own for Week 6. Quinshon Judkins, their star running back, got some bad news on his game-day status.

According to ESPN's Adam Schefter , Judkins is inactive for the Browns, making for quite the troublesome situation for the Browns' running back room this weekend.

Browns get bad news on RB Quinshon Judkins for Week 6

"Browns RB Quinshon Judkins, who was questionable with an ankle injury, is out today," Schefter reports.

This is some huge news for the Browns, especially considering how banged up their running back room is right now heading into this weekend's Ravens game.

So, now with Judkins out, who is going to lead this backfield in Cleveland? Dylan Sampson was not activated off IR this week despite practicing some, and Raheim Sanders was just placed on IR after Week 5.

That means the Browns' backfield now consists of two options: Jaleel McLaughin, and Audric Estime. It's more likely than not going to be a split backfield, with both running backs earning their fair share of work.

Both are former Denver Broncos running backs, though McLaughlin is the only RB to actually see playing time in the NFL regular season. He ran for 31 yards on two attempts for the Browns this season, including a 28-yard touchdown.

McLaughlin is a pass-catching running back and is more likely than not going to be the lead back this week. But the big news here is that, for at least one weekend, the Browns are going to be without their star running back, with Judkins inactive for Week 6.

The Tide are reeling after back-to-back losses to Georgia and Tennessee. Alabama got off to a 5-0 start, but things have obviously cooled down for Kalen DeBoer and company. The Tide's win over Kentucky has aged well, and Alabama looked dominant against both Mississippi State and South Carolina, but two losses in a row can shake a team's confidence. The all-time series is 13-3 in favor of Alabama, though the two teams haven't met since the Elko era began in College Station.

Texas A&M is more than a two-touchdown dog for a reason. Though the Aggies won big against The Citadel and Bama has lost back-to-back games, the Tide are still one of the best teams in the SEC. Linebacker Jaylon Carlies (ribs) and wide receiver Ashton Dulin (hamstring) were ruled out on Friday. Both players missed last week's game as well.

Without Carlies, Bryce Boettcher got the start against the Steelers, but Austin Ajiake was rotated in as well, while CJ Allen saw a career-high 24 defensive snaps.

At wide receiver, Laquon Treadwell filled in for Dulin. In the return game, Anthony Gould has provided depth there.

Tucker and Leonard have been inactive in each game this season.

Cornerbacks Sean Murphy-Bunting and Terell Smith will watch from the sidelines, along with rookie running back Eli Heidenreich.

Murphy-Bunting previously played for the Buccaneers along with Steelers teammate Jamel Dean, who makes his return to Raymond James Stadium after signing a free agent deal to join Pittsburgh in the offseason.

Veteran tailback Rico Dowdle (toe) could be back in the fold with Jaylen Warren, who starred for the Steelers last week and scored two long touchdowns.

Undrafted rookie defensive tackle Kevin Jobity Jr. will have to wait to make his NFL debut.

Rookie third-round pick Drew Allar , who hasn't had a helmet for a game this season yet, also won't suit up, with Will Howard serving as Mike McCarthy's emergency No. 3 quarterback.

Receiver Ben Skowronek, whose calf ailment will keep him out and added to the team's woes at wideout, wasn't placed on injured reserve, unlike Michael Pittman Jr. (foot) and Roman Wilson (finger/hand).

The Steelers will have receiver DK Metcalf and tight end Pat Freiermuth, who popped up on the injury report later in the week with an illness and a calf issue, respectively.

articles.title: Giuntoli: ‘Atalanta want clear identity under Sarri, but it’s a process’
articles.summary: Atalanta director Cristiano Giuntoli admits they ‘want to find a clear identity’ under coach Maurizio Sarri, with more changes for the trip to Milan.It kicks...
articles.body:
Atalanta director Cristiano Giuntoli admits they 'want to find a clear identity' under coach Maurizio Sarri, with more changes for the trip to Milan.

It kicks off at San Siro at 17.00 UK time (18.00 CEST).

The absentee list remains lengthy, as Giacomo Raspadori suffered a muscular strain in Thursday's Conference League match , joining Franck Kessie, Giorgio Scalvini, Odilon Kossounou, Isak Hien and Kamaldeen Sulemana on the treatment table.

Eljif Elmas is also suspended today after his red card against Venezia.

Coach Maurizio Sarri and director Cristiano Giuntoli (@atalanta_bc)

"We have a very deep squad with talented players, so we still maintain this is a competitive side," Giuntoli told Sky Sport Italia.

"Unfortunately, many of the injuries are focused on the same area of the pitch, specifically in defence. We're coming off two good victories and want to see consistency in the performances as well as the results."

Atalanta had a difficult start to the campaign, perhaps inevitable considering Sarri's style of football is so vastly different to that of his predecessors in Bergamo.

He seems to have found their identity in the last couple of matches, beating both Venezia and Conference League opponents Pafos 3-1.

BERGAMO, ITALY – OCTOBER 15: Atalanta BC players applaud the fans after the UEFA Conference League 2026/27 League Phase MD1 match between Atalanta BC and Pafos FC at Stadio di Bergamo on October 15, 2026 in Bergamo, Italy. (Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images)

"We want to find a clear identity, the coach has a lot of experience and has evaluated some things, we tried the 4-3-3, the 4-2-3-1, but the attitude of the lads is ultimately the most important thing," added Giuntoli.

"The result then can be dictated by many different variables, but that mentality has to be consistent."

Lazar Samardzic told Sky Sport Italia today that they have "started playing the kind of football the coach wants to see," but Atalanta's expectations are lowered by the timing of such a radical change on the bench.

BERGAMO, ITALY – SEPTEMBER 12: Lazar Samardzic of Atalanta BC reacts during the Serie A match between Atalanta BC and Parma Calcio at Stadio Atleti Azzurri d'Italia on September 12, 2026 in Bergamo, Italy. (Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images)

"It is certainly a year where we need to find our identity," noted Giuntoli.

"You can call it starting from scratch, Year Zero, a season of adjustment, but we started with play-offs in August for the Conference League, it has been a packed schedule and there hasn't been much time to work in training.

"We're coming off two victories, we had some bad results before, and it is a process."

articles.title: Phil Parker raves about Iowa football DL Bryce Hawthorne
articles.summary: Iowa's defensive coordinator had great things to say about the fourth-year defensive lineman.
articles.body:
The Iowa defensive line underwent a lot of change this offseason.

Longtime stalwarts like Aaron Graves, Max Llewellyn, and Ethan Hurkett all left for the NFL, officially running out of eligibility. Their departures left the Hawkeyes in a difficult spot. Defensive coordinator Phil Parker had a lot of work to do to replace that production. His job was made a bit easier by the return of Bryce Hawthorne.

The Osseo, Minn., native was the only returning defensive lineman with starting experience at Iowa . In 2025, he had 15 total tackles and an interception, playing mostly as a reserve.

Hawthorne was thrust into a starting spot this season, and he's excelled. The 6-foot-3 lineman has 19 total tackles and 2.5 sacks at the halfway point. He's tied with linebacker Preston Ries for the second-most sacks on the team.

Iowa held its midseason coordinators' interviews on Tuesday, and Parker had glowing things to say about what Hawthorne has brought to the table this season.

"We showed a clip a couple days ago of Bryce actually making a great effort play on the sideline. We had a missed tackle in the flat right in front of our bench, and you saw Bryce start running after him. It was the way he's grown a little bit, the effort that he was putting in, and the leadership. He's hard to block, as you see, and he's very active. When somebody does that, it establishes that leadership role. That kid is playing very hard and going full speed all the time, and people respect that. I think he's really done a good job getting back healthy and playing well," Parker said of Hawthorne.

Hawthorne's hustle and effort on every play have earned him a lot of respect from his coaching staff and teammates. He's the kind of player who inspires everyone else to give that extra effort in the biggest moments. That type of leadership can't be taught.

With all of their goals still in front of them this season, the Hawkeyes will lean on Hawthorne's experience to guide a young defensive line. That group has already seen a big leap from Week 1 to now. It's fair to expect them to be even better after the bye week.

articles.title: Buccaneers announce seven are inactive for Week 6 vs. Steelers
articles.summary: Tampa Bay will be without Baker Mayfield, Sean Tucker, Antoine Winfield Jr. and four other players against Pittsburgh.
articles.body:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers will be without several players for Sunday's Week 6 matchup against the Pittsburgh Steelers, including running back Sean Tucker, whose availability remained uncertain heading into game day.

According to Buccaneers Communications , Tampa Bay has announced seven inactive players ahead of kickoff at Raymond James Stadium. Tucker joins quarterback Baker Mayfield, safety Antoine Winfield Jr. and cornerback Benjamin Morrison among those unavailable against Pittsburgh.

Tucker was listed as questionable with a quad injury after missing Wednesday's practice and participating in a limited capacity on Thursday and Friday. Head coach Todd Bowles had indicated that Tucker would be evaluated before Sunday's game, but the final inactive list confirms he will not play. His absence leaves Tampa Bay without another option in the running game as the Buccaneers look to build on last week's victory over Dallas.

Mayfield will miss his third consecutive game with a right thumb injury, leaving rookie Jalon Daniels under center once again. Veteran Easton Stick was elevated from the practice squad Saturday to provide depth behind Daniels.

The Buccaneers will also be without Winfield, who continues to recover from a rib injury, and Morrison, who was listed as doubtful on Friday with a quad injury. Both absences affect a Tampa Bay secondary preparing to face Pittsburgh quarterback Aaron Rodgers.

There is some encouraging news for the defense. Rookie linebacker Josiah Trotter, who appeared on Friday's injury report with a knee issue, has been cleared to play. SirVocea Dennis is also available after missing the previous game with ankle and foot injuries, according to Scott Smith of Buccaneers.com .

Tampa Bay also elevated running back Josh Williams from the practice squad Saturday, providing another backfield option with Tucker unavailable.

Buccaneers inactive players vs. Steelers

The Buccaneers enter Sunday's game at 1-4 and are looking for their second consecutive victory. With Tucker joining Mayfield on the sidelines, Tampa Bay will have to make another adjustment offensively, while the returns of Trotter and Dennis provide some much-needed help on defense.

articles.title: Green Bay Packers react to the Brewers’ World Series berth
articles.summary: Matt LaFleur walked into his Friday press conference wearing a Milwaukee Brewers hat. The Green Bay Packers coach was there to talk about Sunday night’s game...
articles.body:
Matt LaFleur walked into his Friday press conference wearing a Milwaukee Brewers hat. The Green Bay Packers coach was there to talk about Sunday night's game against the Dallas Cowboys, but he started with baseball.

The Milwaukee Brewers beat the Los Angeles Dodgers 6-4 on Thursday night at Dodger Stadium to finish a four-game sweep in the National League Championship Series, MLB.com reported . Milwaukee will play in the World Series for the first time since 1982 and the first time as a National League club.

"You guys like my hat? It's a little big on my head, but I want to support the Brewers," LaFleur said. "That was pretty cool to watch last night. And I've got a lot of respect for their organization, Coach Murphy. I saw something that Christian Yelich said after the game, postgame, that I thought certainly resonated with me in terms of just what it takes to be successful. And I just think they're a first-class organization. Really happy for them."

LaFleur said he did not see much of the series. The milestone still registered.

"Didn't get to watch a whole lot," LaFleur said. "But it is pretty cool when you have an in-state team to reach the World Series for the first time in 44 years. That's a pretty big deal. Just really happy for those guys."

Cornerback Keisean Nixon watched the clincher with divided loyalties. He named Brewers second baseman Brice Turang as the reason for the happy half.

"I actually was kind of happy but sad at the same time," Nixon said. "My boy Turang is like that, but he's also a Cali boy. But the Dodgers losing kind of hurt my heart."

Zaire Franklin got his first look at American Family Field

Several Packers attended a Brewers playoff game in Milwaukee after the 31-7 win over the Chicago Bears on Oct. 11. Linebacker Zaire Franklin, who grew up a Philadelphia Phillies fan, said it was his first time at the ballpark.

"I'm a huge baseball fan," Franklin said. "So it was just fun being able to go, especially off the win, obviously. Pulling up off the loss would have been terrible. It was just a great environment, man. That was my first time in that park. It was really dope. The fans were super intense. Just like all the other Wisconsin fans that I met, though, they were great and hospitable."

His favorite player is Ryan Howard. Franklin said he played first base growing up and listed the Phillies he followed before the 2008 team that won the World Series.

"I would probably say Jim Thome and Bobby Abreu was the reason I started really liking baseball," Franklin said. "But then, obviously, Jimmy Rollins and that '08 Phillies team, they got my heart for real."

That 2008 Phillies team beat the Brewers in the NL Division Series. A reporter brought up 2008, and Franklin waved it off.

"Come on, don't do me like that," Franklin said.

Tucker Kraft hasn't watched, but says 'Go Brewers'

Tight end Tucker Kraft lives in Green Bay in the offseason. He said he did not grow up with baseball and admitted he had not watched the Brewers this postseason.

"This would be big for the entire state of Wisconsin, especially as we also continue to heat up," Kraft said. "Good luck. Go Brewers. As a kid, there was no baseball team at Timber Lake High School, so we didn't have the resources, I guess. I never really got super into baseball, but it'd be great to see the Brewers' success."

"I haven't watched a single game, sorry to admit that, but they have full support of our team," Kraft continued. "A bunch of guys went down there the other day and watched the game. They had a great time, so just go Brewers."

The Brewers led the majors with 103 wins this season. The Packers (3-2) host the Cowboys at 7:20 p.m. CT Sunday on NBC and Peacock.

articles.title: LOOK: Bears' injured safety Coby Bryant walking without crutches
articles.summary: Bears safety Coby Bryant, who had knee surgery this summer, was spotted walking without crutches before the Falcons game.
articles.body:
The Chicago Bears are gearing up for a Week 6 matchup against the Atlanta Falcons, and there was an encouraging site during pregame as safety Coby Bryant was spotted walking the sideline.

Bryant made the trip to Atlanta for the game, as shared by FOX Chicago's Devan Kane, and was spotted walking without crutches during pregame warm-ups. It's an encouraging sign for the veteran free-agent addition, who suffered a knee injury during training camp that required surgery and delayed his Bears debut.

Bryant was expected to miss four to six months, putting his estimated return around early December, which would be big as Chicago looks to make a playoff push down the stretch. It's certainly an encouraging sign to see Bryant already back with the team and walking, without a noticeable limp, as he makes his way back from injury.

Bryant suffered his injury back on Aug. 3 during a 1-on-1 rep in training camp against tight end Cole Kmet, when he landed awkwardly and was holding his left knee. According to the media, Bryant tried to walk off on his own power, but he eventually carted off the field.

With Bryant sidelined, first-round rookie Dillon Thieneman has been the team's top safety, and arguably their best defensive player through the first five weeks of the season. Cam Lewis and the recently-released Xavier Woods have filled Bryant's spot opposite Thieneman.
